questions.q: What does the first Create Record action do in this lab's New Hire Equipment Request flow?
options: Fires the final notification to the IT fulfillment team
Opens a formal Asset Request record on the asset-management side, populated from data pills off the triggering Request Item
Sends the manager an approval notification
Marks the request as approved
questions.explain: Create Record gives the fulfillment team a dedicated record to work from, separate from the raw catalog submission.

questions.q: Why does Step 2 use approval from a specific individual rather than a group variant?
options: Because group approvals are not supported in Service Catalog flows
Because specific-individual approval is always the default choice
Because exactly one named person — the new hire's manager — has to make the decision
Because the IT fulfillment team must approve as a group
questions.explain: A single named approver (the manager) calls for the specific-individual variant, not a group-anyone or group-everyone approval.

questions.q: What happens on the rejected branch of the If/Else after the approval action?
options: The flow retries the approval action automatically
Update Record marks the request approved anyway
A new Asset Request record is created from scratch
A Notify action tells HR and the requester why, and the flow stops
questions.explain: On rejection, the flow notifies the relevant people and ends rather than continuing to fulfillment.

questions.q: In Step 4, what record does Update Record target, and why is that a clean example of the action?
options: The Asset Request record created in Step 1 — not the flow's original trigger record
The manager's sysapproval_approver record
The original Request Item that triggered the flow
A brand-new record it creates itself
questions.explain: Update Record can target any record reachable in the flow, not only the trigger record — here it updates the record Create Record made earlier.

questions.q: Why is Step 2's manager-approval pattern a strong candidate for a custom reusable action, while Step 1's Create Record is not?
options: There is no real difference — both are equally good candidates
Approval actions are never allowed inside custom actions
Create Record cannot be used inside more than one flow, so it must stay custom
The manager-approval pattern repeats identically across many onboarding flows, while the Asset Request creation is specific to this request type
questions.explain: Lesson 11's rule: logic reused identically across flows (manager approval) is worth centralizing; logic specific to one request type (this particular Asset Request) usually isn't.
